Looking at the data: F3Z01 temperature rose by ~2.0°C in Jul-Dec 2018, but adjacent zones also rose (F3Z02 by +0.86°C, F4Z01 by +0.40°C, F2Z05 by +0.28°C, F2Z09 by +0.01°C, F1Z01 by +0.13°C). Setpoints for F3Z01 did not change. The available streams are only zone air temperature sensors and heating/cooling setpoints.

To distinguish "local load change" (real physical heating in the zone) from "zone sensor fault" (only the sensor reading is off), I would need:
- Airflow/damper/terminal box data for the F3Z01 zone (would differ if actual load changed vs. if just the sensor drifted)
- Electrical energy consumption / plug-load streams for the zone
- Supply air temperature and OA/RA conditions
- An external reference / redundant temperature measurement in the same zone, or outdoor air temperature for normalization

The temperature-sensor-only streams cannot definitively separate a real thermal load rise (which would typically be accompanied by HVAC/energy response) from a sensor reading drift.
